applicability: Thoracic pain without red flags (fracture, osteoporosis, malignancy); evidence extrapolated.
adequacy: Trial of about 6 visits over 2 weeks; continue up to about 18 visits over 6-8 weeks only with objective functional improvement; maintenance care not required for MMI.

applicability: Chronic thoracic pain adjunct; evidence extrapolated.
adequacy: Trial of about 3-6 sessions to show functional improvement; continue up to about 8-12 sessions over 4-8 weeks only with documented gains.

applicability: First-line analgesic.
adequacy: Scheduled trial of about 2-4 weeks at therapeutic dose, or documented intolerance/contraindication; lowest effective dose for shortest duration.

applicability: Acute pain with spasm; short course.
adequacy: Short course of 2-3 weeks or less for acute pain or flare; long-term use is not recommended and not required for MMI.

applicability: Alternative when NSAIDs contraindicated.
adequacy: Optional; scheduled trial of 1-2 weeks at up to 3-4 g/day; absence does not preclude MMI.

applicability: Myofascial pain with documented trigger points, symptoms over 3 months, failed conservative care.
adequacy: Repeat only if 50% or more relief for 6 or more weeks with functional gain; injections no more often than every 2 months, 3-4 or fewer per session.

applicability: Chronic pain with psychosocial contributors.
adequacy: Initial 3-4 sessions over 2 weeks; up to about 6-10 sessions over 5-6 weeks with documented functional improvement.

applicability: Chronic disabling pain after failed conventional care.
adequacy: Continuation beyond 2 weeks requires documented objective gains; total generally 20 full-day sessions (or part-day equivalent) or fewer.

applicability: All patients; most improve non-operatively.
adequacy: Adequate when advice to stay active/avoid bed rest and education are documented alongside active care; not a stand-alone trial.

applicability: Initial care as tolerated; evidence extrapolated from cervical/lumbar radiculopathy.
adequacy: About 10 visits over 8 weeks (typical ODG benchmark) with documented objective functional progress, then fading to HEP; more visits only with measurable gains.

applicability: First-line analgesic.
adequacy: Scheduled trial of about 2-4 weeks at therapeutic dose, or documented intolerance/contraindication; lowest effective dose for shortest duration.

applicability: Optional for neuropathic intercostal radicular pain.
adequacy: Titrate to effective/tolerated dose (e.g., gabapentin 1200-1800 mg/day or pregabalin 150-300 mg/day) for about 4-8 weeks; optional - absence does not preclude MMI.

applicability: Concordant thoracic radiculopathy not responding to conservative care (clinical consensus; thoracic-specific evidence limited).
adequacy: Up to 2 injections in the diagnostic phase; repeat only if 50% or more relief with functional gain/medication reduction for 6-8 weeks; generally no more than 4 per region per year.

applicability: Rarely indicated for radiculopathy alone: intractable pain with concordant imaging after prolonged failed care, or any myelopathy.
adequacy: Adequate once performed and post-op rehabilitation completed. Not required for MMI if not indicated, contraindicated, or declined by an informed patient.

applicability: Mild, stable deficits only, with close neurologic monitoring; manipulation contraindicated.
adequacy: Monitoring trial with serial neurologic exams; progression or no improvement means surgical referral, not more therapy.

applicability: Myelopathy from thoracic disc herniation (clinical consensus; no dedicated evidence-based guideline identified).
adequacy: Adequate once performed and post-op rehabilitation completed. Not required for MMI if not indicated, contraindicated, or declined by an informed patient.

applicability: Myelopathy from dorsal compression (e.g., ossified ligamentum flavum) (clinical consensus).
adequacy: Adequate once performed and post-op rehabilitation completed. Not required for MMI if not indicated, contraindicated, or declined by an informed patient.

applicability: Added when decompression causes or accompanies instability or deformity (clinical consensus).
adequacy: Adequate once performed and post-op rehabilitation completed. Not required for MMI if not indicated, contraindicated, or declined by an informed patient.

applicability: All patients; evidence extrapolated from neck/low back care.
adequacy: Adequate when advice to stay active/avoid bed rest and education are documented alongside active care; not a stand-alone trial.

applicability: All patients.
adequacy: Adequate when a program is taught (usually during PT) and ongoing independent adherence is documented.

applicability: Chronic axial thoracic pain.
adequacy: About 10 visits over 8 weeks (typical ODG benchmark) with documented objective functional progress, then fading to HEP; more visits only with measurable gains.

applicability: Without osteoporosis or other red flags; evidence extrapolated.
adequacy: Trial of about 6 visits over 2 weeks; continue up to about 18 visits over 6-8 weeks only with objective functional improvement; maintenance care not required for MMI.

applicability: First-line medication for flares.
adequacy: Scheduled trial of about 2-4 weeks at therapeutic dose, or documented intolerance/contraindication; lowest effective dose for shortest duration.

applicability: Chronic pain with psychosocial contributors.
adequacy: Initial 3-4 sessions over 2 weeks; up to about 6-10 sessions over 5-6 weeks with documented functional improvement.

applicability: Chronic disabling pain after failed conventional care.
adequacy: Continuation beyond 2 weeks requires documented objective gains; total generally 20 full-day sessions (or part-day equivalent) or fewer.

applicability: Early mobilization as tolerated for stable fractures.
adequacy: Adequate when advice to stay active/avoid bed rest and education are documented alongside active care; not a stand-alone trial.

applicability: Stable, neurologically intact fractures per surgeon preference (TLSO/Jewett); bracing optional per CNS 2019.
adequacy: Worn per treating-surgeon protocol until radiographic healing (typically 6-12 weeks); adequate when bracing is completed with healing documented.

applicability: Baseline analgesic.
adequacy: Optional; scheduled trial of 1-2 weeks at up to 3-4 g/day; absence does not preclude MMI.

applicability: Short-course analgesia as healing and risk profile allow.
adequacy: Scheduled trial of about 2-4 weeks at therapeutic dose, or documented intolerance/contraindication; lowest effective dose for shortest duration.

applicability: Severe acute fracture or post-operative pain; taper promptly.
adequacy: Not a required rung; if used, short course (a few days, generally 7 days or less for acute pain); long-term opioid therapy is not required to establish MMI.

applicability: After stability/healing confirmed or post-operatively.
adequacy: About 8 visits over 10 weeks for non-operative fractures (ODG-style benchmark); continue only with objective gains.

applicability: After instruction in PT.
adequacy: Adequate when a program is taught (usually during PT) and ongoing independent adherence is documented.

applicability: Osteoporotic compression fracture with severe ongoing pain despite optimal analgesia and imaging-confirmed unhealed fracture.
adequacy: Single procedure per fracture level; adequate once performed; not required for MMI.

applicability: Unstable fractures or neurologic deficit needing decompression and stabilization.
adequacy: Adequate once performed and post-op rehabilitation completed. Not required for MMI if not indicated, contraindicated, or declined by an informed patient.
